sessions.phase_label: Visual design review and hero refinement
Webflow implementation, content revisions, and handoff preparation
Site launch, domain connection, and lead-form verification
Post-launch DNS incident and domain-routing recovery

requirements.title: Phase-One Webflow Landing Page
requirements.definition: Build the phase-one public marketing landing page in Webflow, separate from the product application and from individual page-content, navigation, and hosting behaviors.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the core Webflow landing-page artifact and bounded phase-one launch scope; visual details, forms, links, handoff, and domain routing remain independent Requirements.

requirements.title: August 5 Delivery Deadline
requirements.definition: Complete the initial landing-page delivery by August 5, 2026.
requirements.boundary_note: The deadline is an independently actionable delivery constraint rather than an attribute of any particular page behavior.

requirements.title: Clean Minimal SaaS Visual Design
requirements.definition: Present the landing page with a clean, minimal SaaS visual style using the supplied brand identity and an approved overall layout.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers overall aesthetic direction and layout approval; hero copy, hero imagery, motion, responsiveness, and section-specific images can change independently.

requirements.title: No Launch Animations
requirements.definition: Keep the phase-one landing page free of animations.
requirements.boundary_note: Motion can be enabled or disabled independently of the page's broader visual style, so it remains a separate behavioral constraint.

requirements.title: Mobile-Responsive Landing Page
requirements.definition: Ensure the public landing page adapts for mobile devices.
requirements.boundary_note: This requirement is explicit in the project opening description; it is distinct from depicting a phone inside the hero artwork.

requirements.title: Hero Headline and Supporting Copy
requirements.definition: Display the client-selected headline and supporting product explanation in the landing-page hero section.
requirements.boundary_note: Headline and supporting paragraphs form one tightly coupled hero-message mechanism; hero artwork is independently replaceable.

requirements.title: Mobile-Framed Product Hero Visual
requirements.definition: Use a hero graphic that clearly presents the LOTCLIP vehicle sales page on a mobile phone, including representative product images and dealership-action links.
requirements.boundary_note: Phone framing, representative buttons, and product imagery are attributes of one hero-visual mechanism; they are separate from hero text and overall page styling.

requirements.title: Bottom-Section Image
requirements.definition: Use the client-selected replacement image in the lower section of the landing page.
requirements.boundary_note: The lower-page image receives its own replacement decisions and can be changed independently of the hero visual.

requirements.title: Dealer Login Button Placement
requirements.definition: Display the Dealer Login button only in the top-right navigation rather than repeating it throughout the site.
requirements.boundary_note: Button visibility and placement can change independently of its destination URL.

requirements.title: Dealer Login Destination
requirements.definition: Navigate the Dealer Login button to the supplied LOTCLIP administration login URL.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers only the button's navigation target, not its placement or the authentication system behind the external destination.

requirements.title: Early-Access CTA Routing
requirements.definition: Route the Request Early Access call-to-action to the contact-form page.
requirements.boundary_note: CTA navigation is independently testable from whether the destination page exists and whether its form submits successfully.

requirements.title: Contact and Early-Access Page
requirements.definition: Provide a dedicated contact page containing the early-access lead form.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers existence of the destination page; page copy, contact methods, form schema, submission delivery, and inbound CTA routing are separate behaviors.

requirements.title: Form-Only Contact Method
requirements.definition: Use only the lead form on the contact page and omit direct email and phone contact options.
requirements.boundary_note: The permitted contact channels can change independently of the form's fields, copy, and delivery behavior.

requirements.title: Founding Dealer Contact-Page Copy
requirements.definition: Display the supplied Founding Dealer headline and explanatory copy on the contact page without textual defects.
requirements.boundary_note: Headline and body copy are one page-message unit; the form's field schema and submission behavior evolve independently.

requirements.title: Contact Form Field Schema
requirements.definition: Collect first name, last name, phone, email, dealership, city, and comments through the early-access form.
requirements.boundary_note: The listed fields form one configurable input schema; email routing and page copy are separately testable.

requirements.title: Contact Form Lead Delivery
requirements.definition: Deliver contact-form submissions to Ryan@lotclip.com and support@lotclip.com.
requirements.boundary_note: Lead delivery has its own execution test and can fail independently of form rendering, fields, or CTA navigation.

requirements.title: Privacy Policy Page or Section
requirements.definition: Include an accessible Privacy Policy page or section on the public website.
requirements.boundary_note: This legal-content requirement is explicit in the project opening description but has no later message-level evidence in the supplied history.

requirements.title: Cost-Effective Webflow Site Plan
requirements.definition: Use the cheapest suitable Webflow site plan, ultimately identified as the Basic plan.
requirements.boundary_note: Subscription-plan selection is independent of DNS routing and website ownership transfer.

requirements.title: Landing Page Custom-Domain Routing
requirements.definition: Connect the Webflow marketing site to the client-controlled domain destination, later revised to get.lotclip.com.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers where the marketing site resolves; preserving the pre-existing product at the apex and www domains has separate failure and recovery trajectories.

requirements.title: Preserve Product Routing at lotclip.com
requirements.definition: Keep the existing LOTCLIP product available at the apex lotclip.com domain rather than replacing it with the Webflow marketing site.
requirements.boundary_note: The apex product route failed and was restored independently of the marketing-site subdomain and the www alias.

requirements.title: Restore www Product-Domain Routing
requirements.definition: Configure www.lotclip.com in Firebase Hosting so it resolves or redirects to the existing LOTCLIP product.
requirements.boundary_note: The www endpoint remained broken after the apex domain was restored and required a different Firebase-side fix, demonstrating an independent trajectory.

requirements.title: Transfer Site to Client Webflow Workspace
requirements.definition: Transfer the completed Webflow site into the client's account or workspace so the client owns and controls it.
requirements.boundary_note: Ownership transfer remains independently required even if the public site is already functional; account-access logistics alone are not separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Client Site-Editing Tutorial
requirements.definition: Provide a Loom tutorial explaining how the client can make future Webflow site edits.
requirements.boundary_note: The tutorial is an independently requested handoff deliverable; Loom is the client-accepted delivery format replacing the initially requested Google document.
